reviews.text: This place is more concerned with making $ than seeing your pet. The initial “free” exam doesn’t happen in front of you although you select an in office visit, and they won’t see your pet without selling you every plan they have, as well as don’t offer any comprehensive information if you don’t pay $300 for bloodwork and $600 for X-rays. I would not recommend this place at all, and I would highly urge you to take your pet somewhere they will be cared for.

I will say the new kitten program is worth the price especially with the spay. OAN: I never saw a vet the entire year. I know she didn't need to see a vet each visit but I NEVER saw a vet or vet tech the entire year I sent my kitten here not even after the spay. I received a message on my phone. When I went to pick her up from her spay I was told she had fleas. They gave her a capstar. Capstar only kills the live fleas on your pet. I asked if I could buy revolution from them to treat my pet, the young lady told me they didn't sell it. I asked so what do u recommend? I was told OTC Frontline. Which is a joke because Frontline doesn't recommend buying their products OTC because they do not insure they will work unless u purchase them from your veterinarian. After I stated this she recommended a medication via chewy. Once again a medication I would need a Rx for that they wasn't supplying. I asked what medicine they had in house to purchase and I was told none. I'm confused how a "veterinarian" facility doesn't offer flea medication for a pet. Please don't come under my post stating you offer this and that because if that was the case I would've purchased it the day I got her spayed. So if you are ok with NEVER seeing a vet and just dropping your pet off and pick them up with just talking to a staff member this is the place for you and your pet.

On April 16th, 2026 I took my Baby in because I was concerned for his health. They kept him to run some test and x-rays. Diagnosis: Congenital Heart Failure. They prescribe meds and scheduled a 2 week follow up. We return April 30th, he gets checked, I was told meds are working, he should be fine. I asked, what was his life expectancy with the medication, DR. JACKSON proceeded to tell me "He will live a normal life with medication!" They send me home and told me to scheduled an appointment in six months... So the appointment would have been in October, BUT MY BABY PASSED AWAY LAST WEEK. They lie to people and give us false hope. I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS PLACE!

horrible experience. on june 30th i went in for the free first visit coupon since my cat has been itching his face and ears to the point he’s breaking the skin. i went in thinking it might be ear mites. though i booked an appointment for 3pm in room they called me and said they would probably need more time with him. and asked me to drop him off at 10:45am. THEY KEPT HIM FOR 6 HOURS. just to do a dang physical, the ear mite test and vaccines. that does NOT take 6 hours. i dropped him off at 10:40am and it was already around 3:40pm. i called the clinic TWICE! both times no answer. they finally called me back 30 mins later. the vet said he looks healthy and he probably has seasonal allergies and they would prescribe me medication. i am on disability and have no job so i told them that and asked them to write the medication names down so i can purchase it elsewhere. she said “of course, i understand” they told me i could pick up my cat and i did. it was now about 4:30pm. they didn’t tell me anything else, like how he was having an allergic reaction to the vaccines just “here’s loki” and “can i email you the receipt?” i said yes. they didn’t even tell me the after care summary is on their online portal and sent me home. when i took my cat out of the carrier he looked 10x worse than when i dropped him off. he was intensely chewing on his paws, his face looked puffy and he could barely open his eyes. i called the vet again to ask what medication i can give him that i have in the house they said to give him 4mg of children’s benadryl so i did. i only found out he was having an allergic reaction to the vaccines because i googled his symptoms. my cat was THIS close to going into anaphylactic shock and they didn’t have the gull to tell me. and THEN i look at the after visit summary; no medication names and i know why they opted out, because they wanted me to buy it from their pharmacy for 300x how much its worth. don’t go here if you’re on fixed income because they don’t treat you or your pet like they matter. horrible horrible inhumane experience. and i am diagnosed with ocd so my anxiety was off the charts all day along with my poor 7y/o baby’s.

I cannot say enough wonderful things about Dr. Baldwin! From the moment she walked into the exam room, I could tell she genuinely cared about my dog, Seven. She took the time to address every single concern I had without ever making me feel rushed. She explained everything in detail, answered all of my questions, and made sure I understood the “why” behind every recommendation.

We discussed Seven’s arthritis, and she explained how cartilage naturally deteriorates over time while reassuring me that, thanks to his Dasuquin, he has excellent range of motion. She thoroughly examined him and told me his body frame, shoulders, elbows, and skin all look great. She even smiled and said he looks like a little baby instead of a grown dog, which absolutely made my day!

We also talked about Seven’s anxiety. Dr. Baldwin educated me on the research supporting Prozac for dogs with anxiety and explained how it can improve their quality of life. She even shared that her own dog takes Prozac, which made me feel much more comfortable with the treatment plan. She also reviewed how and when to use his trazodone during periods of increased anxiety.

She noticed that Seven’s Cytopoint injection has been working well for his environmental allergies, so she administered another dose and explained what to expect over the next several weeks.

One of my favorite moments was when Seven started crying while we were talking. Instead of brushing it off, she recognized that his anxiety was showing and acknowledged exactly what he was experiencing. That level of compassion meant so much to me.

She also celebrated Seven’s progress after he lost 1.2 pounds and encouraged me to keep up the work I’ve been doing with his diet. It felt like she was just as invested in his health as I am.

Finding a veterinarian who is knowledgeable is important, but finding one who is knowledgeable, compassionate, patient, and genuinely passionate about animals is priceless. Dr. Baldwin exceeded every expectation I had, and I left feeling confident that Seven is in the best hands. I’m so grateful we found her, and I highly recommend her to anyone looking for exceptional veterinary care.

My sweet old man was living in pain but held on to life.. for me. Benfield Pet Hospital, well the staff there, were amazing. They saw me distraught and comforted me. At no point did they rush me. From the second I called to see if I could bring Milo there, to the second I walked out their doors. They made the hardest day for me, just a tad bit easier. They ensured me that we were in good hands and I thank them for it.

I brought my long-haired cat in for care, paying $329 for essentially nothing. They didn't shave her to find/show her wound, didn't perform the tests I requested, and didn't administer vaccines. Instead, they told me her condition was so dire that I should go to an emergency hospital they recommended for $4k-$5k if not to "humanely" put her down.

Devastated and sick with anxiety, I hung up in tears, thinking I was going to lose my pet.

The next day, a second vet provided the care she actually needed. He shaved her, found and cleaned her bite wound, gave her antibiotics, vaccines, and ran the tests—all for a fraction of the cost. She is now perfectly happy, healthy, and acting normal. She even weighed a healthy 9lbs, contrary to the first clinic's claim that she was emaciated.

This clinic operates on a drop-off basis with zero face-to-face vet consultation. They caused immense emotional distress and recommended euthanasia for a completely treatable condition. I cannot recommend against them strongly enough
